title: Rust: Builder Pattern
description: Implement the builder pattern for constructing complex objects with a fluent API.

steps.title: Basic Builder
steps.description: Create a `Person` struct with fields `name: String`, `age: u32`, `email: String`. Create a `PersonBuilder` with chainable `name()`, `age()`, `email()` methods and a `build()` method.
hints: Builder methods return `&mut Self` for chaining.
`build()` constructs the Person, using defaults for missing fields.

verification.failureMessage: Build and print a Person using the builder.

steps.title: Consuming Builder
steps.description: Make the builder methods take and return `self` (consuming) instead of `&mut self`. This allows `Person::builder().name("Bob").age(25).build()` style.
hints: `fn name(mut self, name: &str) -> Self { self.name = Some(name.to_string()); self }`
Methods take ownership of self and return Self.
This prevents reuse of a builder after build.

verification.failureMessage: Build Bob using consuming builder method chain.

steps.title: Required Fields with Panic
steps.description: Add validation in `build()`: panic if name is missing (with a clear error message). Demonstrate building with and without a name.
hints: Call `std::panic::catch_unwind` to safely test the panic.
A good builder tells you exactly what's missing.

verification.failureMessage: Print the error message when building without a name.

steps.title: Builder with Complex Validation
steps.description: Create an `OrderBuilder` for building an `Order` struct with items (Vec<String>), shipping address, and payment method. Validate that at least one item is present. Print the built order.
hints: `struct Order { items: Vec<String>, address: String, payment: String }`
`add_item(mut self, item: &str) -> Self` adds to the items vec.

verification.failureMessage: Build an Order with items and print it.

steps.title: Type-State Builder
steps.description: Create a type-state builder where the type system enforces required fields. Use separate structs for each state (e.g., `EmptyPersonBuilder`, `WithNamePersonBuilder`, `CompletePersonBuilder`).
hints: This moves invalid states to compile-time (zero runtime overhead).

verification.failureMessage: Build a person using the type-state builder and print.
